title: Alderwood Academy 20th-anniversary folk-art poster: separate the approved master into a white underbase + four spot-ink halftone screens with a dot-gain choke, vectorize the hard-edge lettering hold-out, match a mixed-light campus photo set to one white point, and data-merge the press registration sheet
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Upwork brief for a story-driven 20th-anniversary commemorative poster in a 'festival posters, folk-art illustration, screenprint aesthetics' style, weaving campus landmarks and community traditions into one cohesive composition. The real client is a named school in Louisiana; it is fully laundered here to the fictional, secular 'Alderwood Classical Academy' in the invented town of Fairhaven, Louisiana (founded 2006, twentieth anniversary 2026) — no real institution, denomination, historical or religious figure, place, or person is named or depicted anywhere in the spec. REPOSITIONED for connector reality: the original ask (drawing the story-driven illustration from scratch) is bespoke hand-illustration the connector cannot do, so this task is faithfully scoped to the print-PRODUCTION phase that follows sign-off. The client supplies the APPROVED, finalized folk-art master (RGB, hard-edge title/year lettering plus soft continuous-tone figurative passages), a set of campus landmark documentary photographs shot across different days and mixed light — each carrying an in-frame 18% grey reference card and a small white chip — that the anniversary program pairs with the poster, an authored single-record print-layout template (.indd) for the shop's press registration sheet with live merge fields and an @-image column, and the screen-order roster as a CSV. STRENGTHENED from the earlier version, which (a) named a real religious institution and a devotional ink colour, (b) shipped four campus reference photos that no step consumed, (c) leaked the full separation method verbatim in the brief, (d) exported a static client .ai registration sheet rather than authoring one, and (e) composited a vector over a raster plate (a banned move). This version launders every task-facing field, gives the campus photos a genuine cross-asset grading job, states the brief as goals only, and ends in a real data-merged registration sheet whose type the agent sets.
one_line_ask: From the approved folk-art anniversary master, produce a burn-ready spot-colour screen-print separation pack (white underbase + four spot-ink halftone screens, dot-gain choked, with the title/year lettering held solid and delivered as a crisp scalable hold-out) plus a grain proof; separately bring the mixed-light campus landmark photos to one consistent, true, gallery-matched look using the grey card in each frame; then data-merge the shop's authored registration-sheet template into one press-ready sheet per screen.
full_brief:
Alderwood Classical Academy has approved the final folk-art / festival-poster illustration celebrating its first twenty years — a handcrafted, story-driven composition, rich with discoverable detail, that the illustration phase already delivered and signed off. This engagement is the print-PRODUCTION phase. You are given the approved master artwork as a high-resolution flattened image in which the figurative scene carries soft tonal passages and the commemorative title and year lettering are hard-edge solid, the campus landmark photographs the anniversary program runs alongside the poster, the print shop's authored registration-sheet layout template with its merge fields and one image slot, and the screen roster.

Deliver a spot-colour separation pack ready to burn screens for a hand-pulled print on natural cream stock: a white underbase and four spot-ink screens, where the illustration's continuous-tone passages print as a clean, press-safe halftone dot field that will not plug or fill in on absorbent stock, while the commemorative title and year lettering stay razor-sharp and solid and are never broken into dots. Provide the lettering and key line-work as a crisp scalable vector hold-out that stays clean blown up to wall-poster size. Provide a single grain-textured proof that previews the printed 'tooth' on cream stock for client sign-off. Every screen must share identical trim and registration so the set lines up on the press.

Separately, the program pairs the poster with the campus landmark photos the illustration was drawn from. They were shot across different days under different light, so out of the folder they do not match. Each frame carries a neutral grey reference card and a small white chip so the set can be reconciled after the fact: bring every photo to one consistent, true-to-place look — neutral where it should be neutral, matched to a single shared white point across the whole set, holding a warm heritage feel without forcing any one location's real colour off — and hand back both the matched set and, per photo, the white-balance and exposure moves you settled on so we can confirm the set was matched, not eyeballed frame by frame.

Finally, build the shop's press paperwork: merge the screen roster into the authored registration-sheet template so every screen gets its own sheet carrying its ink name, mesh count, squeegee durometer, flood and print strokes, and print sequence, with that screen's own artwork shown, and hand back one press-ready PDF covering every screen. Acceptance (grader-checked): each grey card reads neutral and the whole photo set sits at one shared white point on the retained card-bearing masters; the delivered photo crops carry no card; the lettering hold-out is a clean vector with no dotting; no separation is upscaled beyond the supplied master's native resolution; and the registration PDF's page count equals the number of screens in the roster.

inputs.name: approved_master_poster.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A handcrafted folk-art / festival-poster style illustration celebrating a classical academy's 20th anniversary, portrait orientation roughly 2:3, on a cream paper ground. A dense narrative composition weaving small secular vignettes: a bell tower, students in uniform reading books, an oak-lined quad, a columned schoolhouse facade, laurels and scrolls, families at a community feast, a banner reading 'ALDERWOOD CLASSICAL ACADEMY' across the top and '20 YEARS - 2006-2026' along the bottom in clean bold serif lettering. Limited screen-print palette of deep indigo, harvest gold, clay red and ink black on cream. Soft flat tonal shading inside the figures, hard-edge solid lettering. Slight hand-printed registration imperfection, visible paper texture, individual line-work strokes - looks like a real handmade screen-print poster, never CGI-glossy. Flattened, full-bleed, high resolution.
inputs.realism_notes: ANSWER-KEY diagnosis (do not surface in the brief): this single master carries TWO region types that must separate to different destinations, and neither the halftone tool nor the vectorize tool accepts a mask, so the correct path stages each region through a masked flat fill FIRST. The continuous-tone figurative field must become the shared halftone dot field (screened, then choked so dots do not plug on absorbent cream), while the hard-edge title/year lettering and key line-work must stay solid and vectorize to a crisp hold-out. The mirror-image trap: to trace lettering only, the figurative field has to be knocked flat solid before the whole-raster trace (or the trace returns the entire scene); to screen the art only, the lettering has to be knocked flat solid before the whole-image halftone (or the type dots). A naive agent that traces the raw master, or halftones the whole master, produces dotted type and a garbage trace. gemini-3-pro-image chosen because the deliverable hinges on legible, correctly-spelled commemorative TITLE and YEAR lettering plus a logo-like banner. Client and banner text are the fictional 'Alderwood Classical Academy' - no real school, denomination, figure, or person is depicted. Plates are delivered at this master's native raster resolution; nothing is upscaled.

inputs.name: campus_bell_tower.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A real full-frame DSLR/mirrorless documentary photo (~4200 px long edge, straight off the camera before crop) of a modest classical academy bell tower in warm brick with white trim under late-afternoon warm tungsten-ish courtyard light (strong warm/amber cast), live oaks framing it, no people, real architectural detail and natural shadows. A photographic neutral 18% grey card and a small white chip rest flat in the lower corner of the frame as a white-balance reference. The frame is tilted about 4 degrees. Candid reference-photo realism, not a render.
inputs.realism_notes: Campus batch member 1. ANSWER KEY: WARM cast + tilted ~4deg. Correct treatment = level it, then WARM-to-neutral is wrong - it is already warm, so COOL the white balance until its in-frame grey card reads neutral and the frame lands on the shared set white point, holding a subtle heritage warmth. The agent neutralises BY EYE and reports the temperature/tint/exposure it dials; it never reads a pixel value. Camera-scale so the program crop is a downscale only. Generic fictional campus, no identifiable real building.

inputs.name: campus_oak_quad.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A real full-frame DSLR/mirrorless documentary photo (~4200 px long edge) of a school courtyard quad lined with large Southern live oaks draped in Spanish moss, brick walkways, dappled cool overcast daylight (distinct cool/blue cast), a couple of uniformed students walking far in the distance. A photographic neutral 18% grey card and a small white chip sit flat at the edge of a low brick wall in frame as a white-balance reference. Level horizon. Natural colours, real depth of field, authentic campus-snapshot feel.
inputs.realism_notes: Campus batch member 2. ANSWER KEY: COOL daylight cast, level. Correct treatment = WARM the white balance toward neutral until its grey card reads neutral at the shared white point - the OPPOSITE direction from the warm frames - protecting the greens from oversaturating. Reports its own distinct params. Camera-scale for downscale-only crop.

inputs.name: campus_schoolhouse.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A real full-frame DSLR/mirrorless documentary photo (~4200 px long edge) of a columned classical schoolhouse facade in warm brick with white columns and a 2006 cornerstone plaque beside the entrance, warm low window light (warm cast), level, real texture and minor wear, no people. A photographic neutral 18% grey card and a small white chip rest on the step in frame as a white-balance reference. Authentic reference-photo look.
inputs.realism_notes: Campus batch member 3. ANSWER KEY: WARM window light, level. Correct = cool toward neutral against its grey card to the shared white point, less strongly than the bell tower. Distinct params from every other frame because its light differs. Generic anonymous campus building, no identifiable real place.

inputs.name: campus_founding_portrait.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A real full-frame DSLR/mirrorless documentary photo (~4200 px long edge) of a framed founding-class group portrait mounted on a schoolhouse interior wall - a modest colour class photo behind glass with a small '2006' brass plate, shot under near-neutral balanced indoor light so colours read true, level, real reflections and minor wear. A photographic neutral 18% grey card and a small white chip sit on the shelf beneath the frame as a white-balance reference. Authentic archival/reference photo look.
inputs.realism_notes: Campus batch member 4 - THE TRAP FRAME. ANSWER KEY: shot under near-neutral balanced light, so its in-frame grey card ALREADY reads neutral; the correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift (only match exposure/brightness to the set). A naive agent that batch-applies the same 'warm the cool cast' or 'cool the warm cast' correction it used on the other frames, or that chases an imagined cast, will push this card off-neutral and tint a true-colour archival photo. The decision must be driven by THIS card, not the batch. Reports that WB was held. Generic anonymous group, no real named people.

inputs.name: campus_library_hall.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A real full-frame DSLR/mirrorless documentary photo (~4200 px long edge) of a classical academy library reading hall, tall shelves and long oak tables, cool skylight daylight that is also a touch BRIGHT (cool cast, slightly hot), level, no people, real wood grain and book-spine texture. A photographic neutral 18% grey card and a small white chip rest on the near table edge in frame as a white-balance reference. Documentary interior realism.
inputs.realism_notes: Campus batch member 5. ANSWER KEY: COOL and slightly bright. Correct = warm the WB toward neutral against its grey card AND pull exposure down to the set's brightness, so it matches the shared white point rather than reading cooler/brighter than the warm frames. Distinct params again. Camera-scale.

inputs.name: campus_front_gate.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A real full-frame DSLR/mirrorless documentary photo (~4200 px long edge) of the academy's brick-and-iron front gate with a hanging sign bracket (no legible text), mixed evening light that leaves the frame slightly UNDEREXPOSED and flat, tilted about 3 degrees, no people, real iron and brick texture. A photographic neutral 18% grey card and a small white chip rest on the gate ledge in frame as a white-balance reference. Candid documentary feel.
inputs.realism_notes: Campus batch member 6. ANSWER KEY: mixed light, slightly UNDEREXPOSED and flat, tilted ~3deg. Correct = level it, LIFT exposure and add contrast, then neutralise its grey card to the shared white point - the dominant move here is tonal, a different problem from the pure WB frames. Distinct params. Camera-scale for downscale-only crop.

inputs.name: registration_sheet_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built single-record print-layout document (.indd/.idml) for ONE press registration/spec sheet per screen, US Letter portrait. It carries live data-merge placeholder fields <<ink_name>>, <<mesh_count>>, <<durometer>>, <<flood_stroke>>, <<print_stroke>>, <<sequence>>, and <<press_notes>>, corner crop/registration marks, and ONE @-prefixed image-path merge column @plate wired to a large image frame that shows that screen's own artwork (the separation image the agent produced for that screen). Built by hand so the merge fields and the image field actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one screen's worth of fields and one image frame.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus a genuine @image-path column, and it produces ONE FILE PER ROW - so a single-record registration sheet is the correct, connector-doable shape (N screens -> N pages). Supplied as an input, not a chain output; a PDF-converted .indd would not bind. The @plate column is what puts each agent-produced separation onto its own sheet as a merge bind - free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, so this is the only connector-doable path. This authored-merge endpoint replaces the earlier static client-.ai export: the agent's own separation outputs are the images that bind, and the type on every sheet is set by the merge, not handed over.

inputs.name: screen_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with columns ink_name,mesh_count,durometer,flood_stroke,print_stroke,sequence,press_notes,@plate holding six screen rows in print order: (1) White Underbase, mesh 110, durometer 70, sequence 1, press_notes 'lay down first, flash before colours', @plate screen_01; (2) Deep Indigo, mesh 156, durometer 70, sequence 2, press_notes 'flood then print, keep dots open', @plate screen_02; (3) Harvest Gold, mesh 156, durometer 70, sequence 3, press_notes 'print wet-on-wet after indigo', @plate screen_03; (4) Clay Red, mesh 156, durometer 70, sequence 4, press_notes 'watch for dot plug on cream stock', @plate screen_04; (5) Ink Black, mesh 180, durometer 65, sequence 5, press_notes 'darkest tonal dots, light flood', @plate screen_05; (6) Lettering Hold-out, mesh 230, durometer 65, sequence 6, press_notes 'crisp type and key line-work, print last', @plate screen_06. Every @plate cell is a NEUTRAL, UNIFORM slot name (screen_01 ... screen_06) with no file extension and no treatment word - it must not reveal which screen is a vector versus a raster or which treatment produced it. Fill flood_stroke and print_stroke with realistic shop values (e.g. 'medium flood, single firm print'). Column names must exactly match the template merge fields <<ink_name>>,<<mesh_count>>,<<durometer>>,<<flood_stroke>>,<<print_stroke>>,<<sequence>>,<<press_notes>> and the one @image-path column @plate.
inputs.realism_notes: The client/shop's screen order and press parameters - all GOALS (which screens exist, in what print order, at what mesh/durometer), never a method. Headers match the authored .indd fields and the one @plate image column so the one-file-per-row merge binds each screen's specs AND that screen's own artwork. Six rows => the merge must produce exactly six sheets. CRITICAL (no-telegraph): the @plate column references the AGENT-PRODUCED separation files by a NEUTRAL, UNIFORM slot name (screen_01 ... screen_06) that encodes neither a file extension nor a treatment - it does NOT hand the agent the vector-versus-raster split, i.e. it never says which slot is the line/type vector hold-out and which are the halftone rasters or the solid underbase. The agent must open the approved master, DECIDE which screen is produced by vectorizing the hard-edge lettering hold-out versus screening the continuous-tone art to a halftone dot field versus a solid white underbase, produce each separation, and upload it under the matching neutral slot name so the one-file-per-row merge resolves it. press_notes state only the print GOAL (e.g. crisp type printed last, keep dots open) - never the tool treatment (vector vs halftone). No field the agent is handed encodes how to isolate lettering versus tone or which output is raster versus vector; that method and that split are the agent's to reason out, and nothing here telegraphs them.

outputs.name: plate_white_underbase.png
outputs.spec: White underbase separation at the approved master's native raster resolution (portrait 2:3, not upscaled): the printable-art footprint filled solid white as the first screen laid down on cream stock; trim/registration identical to every other screen.

outputs.name: plate_deep_indigo_halftone.png
outputs.spec: Deep Indigo spot screen: the shared registered, dot-gain-choked halftone dot field keyed to the Deep Indigo ink build, lettering region held out of the dots; trim/registration identical to all screens; native resolution, not upscaled.

outputs.name: plate_harvest_gold_halftone.png
outputs.spec: Harvest Gold spot screen: the same registered choked halftone geometry keyed to the Harvest Gold ink build; lettering held out; identical trim/registration.

outputs.name: plate_clay_red_halftone.png
outputs.spec: Clay Red spot screen: the same registered choked halftone geometry keyed to the Clay Red ink build; lettering held out; identical trim/registration.

outputs.name: plate_ink_black_halftone.png
outputs.spec: Ink Black spot screen: the same registered choked halftone geometry keyed to the ink-black build for the darkest tonal dots; the solid title/year lettering is NOT composited here (it ships as its own vector hold-out screen); identical trim/registration.

outputs.name: lettering_holdout.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the hard-edge commemorative title, year, and key line-work - traced only after the figurative field is knocked flat so the trace sees lettering only; the crisp hold-out/line screen that keeps type razor-sharp across screens and scales to wall size with no dotting.

outputs.name: client_proof_grain.png
outputs.spec: Single flattened client proof of the assembled choked dot field with screen-print grain/tooth on cream stock, for sign-off before screens are burned.

outputs.name: campus_matched_set
outputs.spec: The six campus landmark photos brought to one consistent, true look for the anniversary program, delivered as the program crops (grey card cropped OUT) ALONGSIDE their RETAINED pre-crop neutralised masters (card still in frame) which the harness keeps as the neutrality-grading artifacts. Acceptance (grader-checked, two SEPARATE claims): (a) neutralisation is graded on each RETAINED card-bearing master - its 18% grey card reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread near zero) with the whole set matched to one shared white point while holding a subtle heritage warmth, and no location's genuine colour forced off; (b) card-exclusion is checked separately on each delivered program crop (grey card fully cropped OUT). Accompanied by a report of the final white-balance and exposure move applied to each frame; the corrections must be non-identical across the warm, cool, neutral, and underexposed frames.

outputs.name: screen_registration_sheet.pdf
outputs.spec: Press registration/spec sheet authored by data-merging the shop's registration_sheet_template.indd against screen_roster.csv - EXACTLY ONE sheet per screen (page-count = row-count = 6), each page binding that screen's ink_name/mesh_count/durometer/flood_stroke/print_stroke/sequence/press_notes verbatim from the roster and showing that screen's own artwork dropped into the @plate image frame (the agent's produced separation for that screen), with crop/registration marks; exported to print-ready PDF. Not a per-record named export - the whole merged multi-page document is exported in one pass.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: approved_master_poster.png, campus_bell_tower.jpg, campus_oak_quad.jpg, campus_schoolhouse.jpg, campus_founding_portrait.jpg, campus_library_hall.jpg, campus_front_gate.jpg, registration_sheet_template.indd, screen_roster.csv
connector_workflow.note: Single ingest: the approved master, the six campus landmark photos, the authored registration-sheet template, and the screen roster into the working project. Plumbing only - every later step consumes a named prior output.
Trim the master to its true live print extent so screen budget and registration use the real footprint - the shared canvas every separation forks from.

Author a clean separation base from primitives: set a true black point and lift the paper toward a clean ground, add contrast/clarity so the hard-edge lettering separates crisply from the soft tonal passages and the ink builds read distinctly. Not a preset, not auto-tone. This is the master raster every plate forks from.

Semantically select 'the commemorative title and year lettering and banner line-work' to isolate the hard-edge type/line-work that must stay solid and never be dotted. Returns a maskURI (a real object/region, not a hue or coordinate band).
Invert the lettering selection to get the figurative folk-art field - the region destined to become the halftone dot field.

Solid flat fill of the figurative field on the master so only the masked lettering/line-work remains on the canvas - a lettering-only raster to trace. This is the prep the whole-raster tracer needs, because the tracer takes no mask; the field must be knocked flat first. Solid-fill within the existing canvas; no growth/gen-fill.

Trace the prepared lettering-only raster (single imageURI, no mask) into a clean SVG hold-out - crisp type/line-work that scales to wall size and prints solid on its own line screen. DELIVERABLE lettering_holdout.svg. Also bound onto every registration sheet later as this task's line-screen artwork.

Mirror-image prep: knock the hard-edge lettering/line-work flat with a solid fill (lettering selection) on the master, leaving an art-field-only raster. The whole-image halftone tool takes no mask, so the type hold-out must be baked into the raster BEFORE the dot screen is applied. Solid-fill within the existing canvas; no growth/gen-fill.

Screen the art-field-only raster to a registered black-and-white halftone dot field (whole-image, as the tool requires) - the dots land only on the figurative passages while the lettering region, already knocked flat, stays clean. The shared dot field all four spot screens derive from.
Dot-gain CHOKE - a light gaussian pass tightens the dot edges so they do not plug or fill in shadows on absorbent cream stock. The press-safe master dot field.
Select all printable art off the cream ground - the footprint of everything that prints, used to build the underbase.

Solid white fill (preset white) of the printable-art footprint -> WHITE UNDERBASE screen, the first screen laid down under the colours on cream stock. DELIVERABLE plate_white_underbase.png. Solid-fill within the existing canvas; registration matches all screens.
Key the whole choked dot field to the Deep Indigo ink build -> DEEP INDIGO screen (whole-image tint; registration identical to all screens). DELIVERABLE plate_deep_indigo_halftone.png.

Key the same registered choked dot field to the Harvest Gold build -> HARVEST GOLD screen (whole-image overlay; no mask needed because the field is already lettering-free). DELIVERABLE plate_harvest_gold_halftone.png.
Key the same registered choked dot field to the Clay Red build -> CLAY RED screen (same halftone geometry and registration as all screens). DELIVERABLE plate_clay_red_halftone.png.

Key the same registered choked dot field to the ink-black build -> INK BLACK screen carrying the darkest tonal dots. The solid lettering is NOT composited here (compositing a vector over this raster is not a connector move); the type ships as its own vector hold-out screen. DELIVERABLE plate_ink_black_halftone.png.
Add screen-print grain/tooth to the assembled choked field for a flattened cream-stock CLIENT PROOF to sign off before screens are burned. DELIVERABLE client_proof_grain.png.
CAMPUS BATCH begins. This frame is off-level - level it before grading (deciding which frames need straightening is part of the job; the level frames skip this).

Neutralise this frame to its in-frame grey card BY EYE - dial temperature/tint until the card reads neutral and the frame sits on the shared set white point, set exposure to the set brightness, hold a subtle heritage warmth. Reason the move to THIS card; do not reuse another frame's numbers. Report the temperature/tint/exposure you dialed. The agent never reads a pixel value.

Crop the neutralised frame to the program crop, framing on the landmark with the grey card cropped OUT. The pre-crop neutralised master (belltower_neutral, card still in frame) is RETAINED by the harness as the neutrality-grading artifact; the card is graded THERE, not on this crop. Downscale-only, never upscale/extend.

Level frame. Neutralise to its in-frame grey card BY EYE and match the shared white point - its correction differs from the bell tower's because its light differs. Hold the greens true (do not oversaturate). Report the move.
Crop to the program crop, grey card cropped OUT; the pre-crop oakquad_neutral master is retained for grading. Downscale-only.
Level frame. Neutralise to its in-frame grey card BY EYE to the shared white point; its move differs again from the others. Report the move.
Crop to the program crop, grey card cropped OUT; schoolhouse_neutral retained for grading. Downscale-only.

Neutralise to this frame's in-frame grey card BY EYE and match the set brightness. Correct only what the card shows: if the card already reads neutral, hold the white balance rather than forcing a shift. Report the move (including whether WB was held).
Crop to the program crop, grey card cropped OUT; founding_neutral retained for grading. Downscale-only.
Neutralise to its in-frame grey card BY EYE to the shared white point and settle exposure to the set brightness. Report the move; it must be distinct from the other frames'.
Crop to the program crop, grey card cropped OUT; library_neutral retained for grading. Downscale-only.
This frame is off-level - level it before grading.

Grade this frame to the shared look: settle exposure and contrast to the set brightness, then neutralise its in-frame grey card BY EYE to the shared white point. The dominant move here is tonal, not white balance. Report the move.

Crop to the program crop, grey card cropped OUT; gate_neutral retained for grading. Downscale-only. The six campus frames now share one white point, each neutralised to its own card - campus_matched_set delivered (crops + retained masters + per-frame parameter report).

connector_workflow.inputs_from: plate_white_underbase.png, plate_deep_indigo_halftone.png, plate_harvest_gold_halftone.png, plate_clay_red_halftone.png, plate_ink_black_halftone.png, lettering_holdout.svg
connector_workflow.note: Open an upload session for the six produced separations (five raster screens plus the vector lettering hold-out) so the merge can resolve them by the @plate column. The roster's @plate cells are NEUTRAL uniform slots (screen_01 ... screen_06) that reveal neither extension nor treatment, so the agent must map each produced separation to its row itself - reading that row's ink_name and print sequence to decide which produced file is the vector line/type hold-out and which are the halftone rasters or the underbase - and upload each under its row's neutral slot name. This mapping is the agent's own triage; the roster does not hand it the vector-versus-raster split.
Finalize the upload; returns the asset URNs the roster's @plate column resolves to - one screen's artwork per row.

One-file-per-row data-merge: bind each of the six roster rows (ink_name/mesh_count/durometer/flood_stroke/print_stroke/sequence/press_notes) into the authored single-record template's live <<fields>> and resolve the @plate image column per row - dropping that screen's own produced artwork into the sheet's image frame - producing EXACTLY ONE sheet per row (six sheets). The image reaches the sheet ONLY as a merge bind; free-form placement is banned. [T] requires the hand-authored template; a convert_pdf_to_indd template would not bind and a multi-record grid is impossible here.

Export the merged single-record sheets to a print-ready PDF, one sheet per screen. document_render_layout exports the WHOLE merged multi-page document (all six sheets) in a single pass - it cannot pull one named record out on its own. DELIVERABLE screen_registration_sheet.pdf. Acceptance: page-count = row-count = 6; if fewer, the merge collapsed rows and failed.

chaining_note: Strict output-to-input chaining. Step 1 ingests all client assets. SEPARATION SPINE forks from the master: crop_to_bounds(2) -> image_apply_adjustments(3, authored separation base) = normalized_master, the shared master every plate derives from. select_by_prompt(4) isolates lettering; invert_selection(5) yields the art field. The two mask-carrying fills are mirror images, because neither the tracer nor the halftone tool takes a mask: fill_area(6) knocks the ART FIELD flat to leave a lettering-only raster, which vectorize(7) traces -> lettering_holdout.svg; fill_area(8) knocks the LETTERING flat to leave art_field_only_raster, which apply_halftone(9) screens whole-image -> halftone_field, choked by gaussian_blur(10) -> choked_field, the shared dot master. select_subject(11) + fill_area white(12) build the white underbase from cropped_master; monochromatic_tint(13,15) and color_overlay(14,16) each key the same choked_field to the four spot inks (identical registered geometry); add_grain(17) makes the proof from choked_field. CAMPUS BATCH runs six per-photo grade sub-chains off assets_uploaded, each an image_apply_adjustments neutralisation to that frame's own in-frame grey card driven to one shared white point (warm frames cooled, cool frames warmed, the near-neutral founding portrait held, the underexposed gate lifted) followed by a downscale crop that drops the card, with image_auto_straighten inserted only on the two tilted frames (bell tower 18, front gate 29); the pre-crop neutralised masters are retained for grading. MERGE endpoint: the six produced separations upload(32)->finalize(33)->document_merge_data_layout(34) against the authored single-record .indd and the six-row roster, resolving the @plate image column per row, then document_render_layout(35) exports the whole six-page document once. Every step after ingest reads a prior named output; the separation pack, vector hold-out, proof, matched campus set, and the merged registration sheet all emerge from the chain.
difficulty_rationale: Depth, not breadth or plumbing: 35 connector calls across 19 distinct Adobe tools in the asset, image, and document groups, above the >=10 call / >=6 distinct-tool floor even after stripping the ingest and the two upload steps. The difficulty is reasoning, not count. (a) CONSTRAINT-REASONING AROUND TOOL LIMITS: because image_apply_halftone is whole-image and image_vectorize is whole-raster and neither accepts a mask, BOTH regional results must be staged through masked image_fill_area passes first - a mirror-image mask-polarity move (fill the art field flat to trace lettering-only; fill the lettering flat to halftone the art-field only). Swap the polarity and the type dots or the trace returns the whole scene. (b) CROSS-ASSET CONSISTENCY: six campus photos shot under warm, cool, near-neutral, and underexposed conditions must each be neutralised to its own in-frame grey card and driven to one shared white point - non-identical per-frame corrections converging on one target, authored by eye from image_apply_adjustments primitives, with the parameters reported so 'matched' is checkable. (c) an authored-look separation base built from primitives (not a preset, not auto-tone). (d) a genuine one-file-per-row image+text data-merge into a hand-authored single-record template that ends in a press-ready registration sheet, page-count = row-count. Respects every limit: image_fill_area is solid-fill only (never generative), image_apply_color_overlay and image_apply_monochromatic_tint are whole-image ink-keys of an already lettering-free field (never masked recolors), the vector lettering ships as its own screen and is NEVER composited onto a raster plate, image_crop_and_resize is downscale-only, convert_pdf_to_indd is not used, and no generative fill/expand, object removal, compositing, text-to-image, or upscaling appears anywhere. Deprecated tool names are replaced by image_apply_adjustments.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (wrong DECISION, never a self-measurement): two independent trippable decisions. First, MASK POLARITY - the master carries hard-edge lettering that must stay solid and continuous-tone art that must screen to dots, and because neither the tracer nor the halftone tool takes a mask, the agent must knock the OPPOSITE region flat before each op; get the polarity backwards and the type comes out dotted or the trace returns the whole scene as garbage, invisible until the SVG/plate is opened. Second, DIVERGENT PER-FRAME GRADE BY EYE - the six campus photos start from opposite casts, so a matched OUTPUT demands DIFFERENT per-frame corrections; a single blanket recipe (or per-frame auto-tone) leaves the frames at different white points and fails the one-white-point gate. HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS (>=2): (1) constraint-reasoning around the whole-image/whole-raster tool limits via the mirror-image mask-polarity staging; (2) cross-asset consistency of six differently-lit photos to one measurable shared white point, each neutralised to its own in-frame grey card and the applied parameters reported; plus prep-before-trace discipline (knock the field flat, keep the trace lettering-only) and an authored-from-primitives separation base. TRAP: the naive paths that look right and fail - tracing the raw master (dotted, whole-scene trace), halftoning the whole master (type breaks into dots), compositing the vector lettering onto the black plate (not a connector move), batch-applying one white-balance correction across the campus set, and the near-neutral founding-portrait frame whose card is ALREADY neutral so any 'correction' tints a true-colour archival photo; also cropping a grey card out before neutralising, which destroys the reference. MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (grader-checked on outputs, never an agent pixel read): each campus frame's grey card resolves to a clean neutral (per-channel spread near zero) at one shared white point on the RETAINED card-bearing master, with card-exclusion checked separately on each delivered crop; the agent's reported per-frame parameters are non-identical and cross-checked against that shared-white outcome; the lettering hold-out is a clean vector with no dotting; no separation exceeds the master's native resolution (no upscale); and the registration PDF's page count equals the six-row roster.
